summary: William Wilfred Webb (1858–1911) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Aberdeen. He served in the Indian Medical Service (1882), Bengal Army (~1883–1894), and Army Medical School (1893–1902).

William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887), as Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University (1886–1887), and with the Royal Asiatic Society.

William Woodville Rockhill (1854–1914) was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Lycée Condorcet, École spéciale militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873), and under Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux (~1876–1880).

William Wright (1830–1889) studied linguistics at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden. He served as Assistant Keeper at the British Museum (1861–1870) and Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge (1870–1889).

William Yates (1792–1845) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (1812), under William Carey (~1815–1834), and received degrees from Brown University in 1831 and 1839.

Willibald Kirfel (1885–1964) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He worked as a librarian at Bonn University Library (1911–1921) and as Professor of Indology at Bonn (1922–1953).

Willy Bang Kaup (1869–1934) studied linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies at KU Leuven under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin. He taught at KU Leuven, Goethe University Frankfurt (1917), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1918).

Willy Baruch (1900–1954) studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology at Berlin, Leipzig, and Bonn, where he earned his Ph.D. under Willibald Kirfel (~1934–1937). He taught Manchu at INALCO (1933–1935).

Willy Foy (1873–1929) studied Indology and linguistics at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and Karl Brugmann. He served as the first director of the Rautenstrauch-Joest Museum (1901–1925) and as professor at the University of Cologne (1914; 1920–1929).
Willy Zinkgräf (b. 1903) was an Indologist who studied under Max Walleser (1922) and earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (-1939). He held a post at the Walleser-Institut.

Wilt L. Idema (b. 1944) is a Sinologist who completed his degrees at Leiden University under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé. He served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and Harvard University (2000–2013).

Winfred P. Lehmann (1916–2007) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1941). He was a professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986–2007).
Winfred Robert Martin (d. 1915) worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winfried Petri (1914–2000) was an Indology, Tibetology, and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Helmut Hoffmann and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (-1966), where he later served as professor (1971) and director (1977–1979).

Wing-tsit Chan (1901–1994) was a Sinology and philosophy scholar who studied at Harvard (~1924–1929). He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1936–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan (b. 1950) studied religious studies at Cornell and the University of Chicago. Her career includes posts at Washington and Lee University, University of Chicago (2000–2005), University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington (~2012).
Winston Kyan specializes in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago, studying under Hung Wu and Linda Seidel.

Winston L. King (1907–2000) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Asbury, Andover Newton, and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1940). He held faculty posts at Grinnell College, Vanderbilt University, and Colorado State University.

Wladimir Zwalf (1932–2002) worked in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Thomas Burrow at Lincoln College (1952–1955) and held posts at the India Office Records (1957–1962) and the British Museum (1962–1993).

Wm. Theodore de Bary (1919–2017) was a Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology scholar educated at Columbia and Harvard. He served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia University (1953–2017) and president of the Association for Asian Studies (1969–1970).
